entries.name: PL/SQL
entries.definition: Oracle's procedural extension of SQL, used to write stored procedures, functions and triggers in Oracle Database.

entries.name: PL/pgSQL
entries.definition: The procedural language built into PostgreSQL for writing stored functions and triggers.

entries.name: Polish
entries.definition: A West Slavic language, the official language of Poland.

entries.name: Portuguese
entries.definition: A Romance language spoken in Portugal, Brazil and several other countries.

entries.name: PostScript
entries.definition: A stack-based page description language and programming language from Adobe, used to describe printed pages and graphics.

entries.name: Power Fx
entries.definition: A low-code formula language from Microsoft, modelled on Excel formulas, used in Power Apps and the Power Platform.

entries.name: PowerShell
entries.definition: A Microsoft command-line shell and scripting language built on .NET, used for task automation and configuration management.

entries.name: Prolog
entries.definition: A logic programming language in which programs are written as facts and rules and run by answering queries.

entries.name: Punjabi
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Punjab region of India and Pakistan.

entries.name: PureScript
entries.definition: A strongly typed, purely functional programming language that compiles to JavaScript.

entries.name: Python
entries.definition: Writing programs in Python.

entries.name: Q#
entries.definition: A Microsoft programming language for expressing quantum algorithms.

entries.name: Quechua
entries.definition: A family of Indigenous languages spoken in the Andes of South America, of which Southern Quechua has the most speakers.

entries.name: R
entries.definition: A programming language and software environment for statistical computing and graphics.

entries.name: Racket
entries.definition: A general-purpose programming language in the Scheme and Lisp family, designed to support creating new languages.

entries.name: Romanian
entries.definition: A Romance language spoken mainly in Romania and Moldova.

entries.name: Ruby
entries.definition: A dynamic, object-oriented scripting language created by Yukihiro Matsumoto and known for its readable syntax.

entries.name: Russian
entries.definition: An East Slavic language, the official language of Russia.

entries.name: Rust
entries.definition: A systems programming language focused on memory safety, concurrency and performance, without a garbage collector.

entries.name: Sakha
entries.definition: A Turkic language spoken mainly in the Sakha Republic in the Russian Far East.

entries.name: Samoan
entries.definition: A Polynesian language, an official language of Samoa.

entries.name: Sango
entries.definition: A language of the Central African Republic, used as a lingua franca and an official language alongside French.

entries.name: Santali
entries.definition: An Austroasiatic language spoken by the Santal people of eastern India, Bangladesh and Nepal.

entries.name: Saraiki
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken mainly in the south of Punjab province in Pakistan.

entries.name: SAS
entries.definition: The programming language of the SAS software suite, used for data management, statistical analysis and reporting.

entries.name: SAS macro language
entries.definition: The text-substitution language in SAS that generates and controls SAS code through macro variables and macros.

entries.name: Sass
entries.definition: A stylesheet language that extends CSS with variables, nesting and mixins and is compiled into ordinary CSS.

entries.name: Scala
entries.definition: Writing programs in Scala.

entries.name: Scheme
entries.definition: A minimalist dialect of Lisp with lexical scoping and first-class continuations.

entries.name: Scratch
entries.definition: A block-based visual programming language developed at the MIT Media Lab for teaching children to code.

entries.name: Serbo-Croatian
entries.definition: A South Slavic language whose standardized forms include Bosnian, Croatian, Montenegrin and Serbian.

entries.name: Service Provisioning Markup Language
entries.definition: An OASIS XML-based standard for exchanging user, resource and service provisioning information between systems.

entries.name: Sesotho
entries.definition: A Bantu language, the national language of Lesotho and one of the official languages of South Africa.

entries.name: Shan
entries.definition: A Tai language spoken by the Shan people, mainly in Shan State, Myanmar.

entries.name: Shell scripting
entries.definition: The scripting languages of Unix command-line shells such as sh and Bash, used to automate sequences of commands.

entries.name: Shona
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken mainly in Zimbabwe.

entries.name: Silesian
entries.definition: A West Slavic language spoken in Upper Silesia, mainly in southern Poland.

entries.name: Simula
entries.definition: An early object-oriented programming language developed in the 1960s by Ole-Johan Dahl and Kristen Nygaard that introduced classes and objects.

entries.name: Sindhi
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Sindh province of Pakistan and parts of India.

entries.name: Sinhala
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language, the main language of Sri Lanka.
